headline: Isolation and identity crises: For injured NHLers, the mental grind is worse than the physical
take:
The Athletic reports on the mental toll of injuries, with the Avalanche's Gabriel Landeskog and Golden Knights' Jack Eichel describing how time away from the game affected their sense of identity. Neither player is listed as out right now, but both have returned to look like themselves.

Landeskog has four goals and six points in 10 games so far this season, and COL has had 55.89% of the 5-on-5 expected goals (a measure of chance quality) with him on the ice. His own expected goals are 2.45, so his four goals are 1.55 above what his chances suggest, and some of that scoring may cool off. Eichel has 18 points in 11 games, and VGK's 5-on-5 expected goal share is 59.58% with him playing, 7.91 percentage points better than without him. His goals are 1.73 above expected, but the playmaking and territorial impact look real.

If either has to miss time, going by how the coach has used his players, T.J. Hughes is next in line for Landeskog's minutes, and Mark Stone for Eichel's, with Braeden Bowman the likeliest to move up on the power play.
